subject: Urgent: GPU pool headroom drain + reserved throughput mismatch (AuroraFin)
messages:
From: Sam Rodriguez <s.rodriguez@aurorafin.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: AuroraFin SRE <ops@aurorafin.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production degradation — high latency and 5xx spikes affecting checkouts

Markus,

We started seeing elevated latency and 5xx errors across our checkout flows at ~08:45UTC. P95 latencies jumped from ~200ms to >2s and throughput dropped ~35% compared to our baseline. This coincides with a sharp increase in GPU queue depth on your side (we shared the sample trace attached). Our customer success team is fielding calls and this is impacting revenue today.

Can your team confirm whether AuroraFin's reserved capacity is being rate-limited or if noisy neighbor activity is impacting our pool? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for reduction in error rates.

— Sam
AuroraFin — Head of Platform

Attachments: aurorafin_error_snapshot.log, throughput-metrics-20261107.csv

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sam Rodriguez <s.rodriguez@aurorafin.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Production degradation — high latency and 5xx spikes affecting checkouts

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We see the same signals in our monitoring: an unexpected burst driving steady-state queueing in the dedicated GPU pool assigned to AuroraFin. 

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Spun up emergency burst nodes to give short-term headroom (ETA 7–10m).
- Temporarily increased reservation weight for AuroraFin to prioritize your traffic while we diagnose.
- Engaging infra to look for noisy-neighbor patterns and to validate kernel-level contention.

I'll loop in David and Priyom for root cause + follow-up. We'll confirm a remediation path within the hour. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as P1.

— Markus
VP, Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T09:39:00Z
Subject: Re: Production degradation — quick signal triage and temporary controls

Markus / Priyom — quick notes from infra:
- Telemetry shows AuroraFin's token rates spiked 2.4x starting 08:40UTC; tail-kv-cache evictions increased substantially and that amplified per-token CPU work.
- A recent model variant (q8-lite) rollout to a small percentage of requests in that pool coincided with the spike; kernel profiles show higher memory-pressure for that variant.

Recommended immediate mitigations (we can enact now):
1) Revert the q8-lite variant routing for AuroraFin to the prior quantization (q4-main) for all canary traffic.
2) Enable per-customer request shaping at the router to cap burst concurrency at 1.5x baseline for 2 hours.
3) Add temporary capacity (we already started burst) and shift non-critical background workloads off the pool.

I'll attach the kernel trace and the extracted metrics to the ticket (JIRA-INC-8892). If quantization variant is the root cause, we should schedule a controlled regression test rather than revert blindly.

— David
Head of Platform Reliability

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production degradation — proposal for customer-facing remediation and exec note

Folks,

Summary of status at 11:00UTC: burst nodes live, error rate down ~60% from peak, latency p95 reduced to ~700ms (still above SLA). Kernel analysis points to q8-lite memory working set causing cache churn in shared allocators — noisy neighbor exacerbated by a transient increase in AuroraFin's request horizon.

Customer asks we should address now:
- Public-facing ETA to full recovery (AuroraFin wants an hour estimate).
- Compensation/credit ask if we can't return to SLA within 24 hours.

Proposed communication to AuroraFin (to send from Markus):
- Acknowledge incident, list immediate mitigations taken, share short-term ETA (target: 2–4 hours for stable p95 < 250ms) and offer a one-time service credit if we miss a 24h SLA.
- Commit to a technical postmortem within 72 hours and a mitigation roadmap (isolation by tenant, quant-variant vetting, enhanced per-tenant cache quotas).

Irene — we should evaluate whether to request executive attention for priority capacity if stabilization does not reach target in 3 hours.

— Priyom
Director, Incident Response

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sam Rodriguez <s.rodriguez@aurorafin.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T18:35:00Z
Subject: Incident update — provisional resolution and next steps (AuroraFin)

Sam — quick update and next steps after today's escalation: 

What happened (brief):
- On 2026-11-07 at ~08:40UTC AuroraFin experienced a burst in request volume that coincided with a limited rollout of the q8-lite quantized variant to a fraction of traffic in the shared dedicated pool. The q8-lite working set increased KV eviction pressure and caused queueing across the pool.

What we did (immediate):
- Reverted q8-lite routing for your tenant and reconfigured per-tenant cache quotas.
- Brought up emergency burst capacity and shifted background batch jobs off the pool.
- Enabled request shaping at the edge to smooth concurrency spikes.

Current status:
- Error rate is within normal bounds; p95 latency is trending toward SLA but we are still monitoring (current p95 ~240ms as of 18:20UTC).

Commitments and asks:
- We will deliver a full postmortem within 72 hours (root cause, timeline, and long-term mitigations).
- If we cannot meet SLA stability within 24 hours from initial incident, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit tied to the reserved-capacity agreement (DF-4521).
- Proposed longer-term fixes: per-tenant allocator isolation, model-variant safety gates before rollouts, and a dedicated reserve headroom policy for top-tier customers.

Naomi — please prepare the exec note and a concise slide (1–2 slides) for CS and our sales leadership summarizing impact, remediation, and proposed credits. Irene — please liaise with Infrastructure for the allocator isolation ETA. Priyom — keep the JIRA ticket updated (JIRA-INC-8892) and draft the postmortem skeleton.

Sam — sorry again for the outage and thank you for working with us. I will keep you posted hourly until we declare the incident closed.

Best,
Markus
VP, Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
